text:
Maria (PM): Quick intake from ACME Retail — they need predictable embeddings throughput for a search/recos feature. Ask: Dedicated deployment with burstable GPU pool. Rough targets they gave: sustained 50k embeddings/min, 5k/sec normal peak, 20k/sec bursts for ~10 minutes. Also want 99.9% availability and p95 latency goal around 1s. Please triage for sizing + rollout criteria.

Kevin (Sales): They also pushed a cost target: <$0.0006 per embedding. Can we meet that with Dedicated?

Sanjay (Eng): Need to know the model variant. If they use a smaller open embedding model (quantized) throughput is much higher. If it's a large model, numbers explode. Any idea which model?

Maria (PM): ACME said "redwood-open-embed-v1" (quantized) for now, maybe switch later. They want the option to fallback to hosted smaller model.

Ellie (Runtime): Quick back-of-envelope: redwood-open-embed-v1 at batch sizes ~256 gives ~1.2k embeds/sec per A100-ish on our runtime. To hit 20k/sec bursts we'd need ~17 GPUs active. For sustained 5k/sec ~5 GPUs. Warm-up time matters — cold scale from 5->17 will take time. Suggest reserved warm pool + autoscale.

Jordan (Support): FYI customer says tail latency can be up to 5s but p95 should be near 1s. That's a tough trade.

Amy (Sales): I'll negotiate p95 to 1.5s if it buys them cost reduction.

Sanjay (Eng): Proposed sizing + policy:
- Dedicated pool min: 4 GPUs (keeps steady 5k/sec with headroom)
- Burst reserve: 4 GPUs hot (immediately available)
- Autoscale max: 20 GPUs
- Warmup: synthetic traffic ramp for 15m before scheduled marketing peaks

Suggested rollout acceptance tests:
1) Perf test: synthetic traffic at 20k/sec sustained for 10m in prod-like env, verify p95 <= 1.5s.
2) Canary: 5% of real traffic for 24h, verify error rate <0.1% and cost per embed within 10% of estimate.
3) Fallback: automatic routing to hosted smaller model if latency or capacity breached.

Ellie (Runtime): Autoscale config draft (we can tweak):
```yaml
autoscaling:
  min: 4
  max: 20
  target_rps_per_gpu: 1200
  scale_up_cooldown: 30s
  scale_down_cooldown: 300s
  burst_reserve: 4
  prewarm_policy: synthetic_warmup_15m
```

Sanjay (Eng): Also need to account for KV cache warm-up. Prepopulate commonly requested prefixes from their prod sample to avoid cold-cache penalty on burst.

Kevin (Sales): If we go with this, what's rough cost estimate? Even a ballpark will help negotiations.

Ellie (Runtime): Ballpark GPU-hours for a baseline month with some burst days: assuming average 6 GPUs (= sustained + some bursts amortized) -> ~432 GPU-hours/day -> monthly ~13k GPU-hours. I know it's broad but gives order of magnitude.

Amy (Sales): I'll flag to ACME they may need to accept slightly higher p95 or add reserved capacity to reduce cost.

DeployBot: Canary job created: job/emb-sim-2165432100, perf harness scheduled.

Maria (PM): Great. I'll file a backlog ticket with acceptance criteria above and tag engineering. Action items: @Sanjay run perf sims and finalize min/max, @Ellie write warmup playbook + autoscale knobs, @Amy/ @Kevin confirm SLA/cost flexibility with ACME. Target: EOD Friday to have estimates. :thumbsup:

Sanjay (Eng): Acknowledged — will run sims tomorrow morning and post numbers here.

Ellie (Runtime): I'll draft the warmup steps and a short playbook for canary/fallback procedures.

Kevin (Sales): I'll push the cost/SLA options today.

Jordan (Support): I'll prepare a support runbook for failover to hosted models and notify on-call.

Maria (PM): Thanks everyone. I'll add the backlog item and link perf job once DeployBot finishes.
